To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exercise training after uncomplicated myocardial infarcts improves functional capacity, but does not improve myocardial perfusion.
the improvement in exercise capacity that occurs within 6 months after a clinically uncomplicated AMIs does not appear to be related to changes in myocardial blood flow or left ventricular function.

the increase in functional capacity (peak exercise workload) that occurs 3 to 6 months after uncomplicated acute myocardical infarction is significantly correlated with the change in peak exercise heart rates, but not with changes of myocardial perfusion, or left ventricular function determined by radinuclide techniques.

exercise training improves functional capacity after acute myocardial infraction (AMI) but does not improve myocardial perfusion, ejection fraction, or left ventricular function.
